mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an infinite set?

options.A: A set that contains a finite number of elements.
options.B: A set that contains exactly one element.
options.C: A set that contains no elements.
options.D: A set that contains an unbounded number of elements, i.e., not finite.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains an unbounded number of elements, i.e., not finite.
mcqs.explanation: An infinite set is one that is not finite; it has no last element and its elements cannot be counted to a finite total. Option D captures this definition. Option A describes a finite set, B a singleton set, and C the empty set, none of which are infinite.

mcqs.question: A set that contains exactly one element is called a:
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set has precisely one element, which is the definition of a singleton. The empty set (A) has no elements, a finite set (C) can have any finite number of elements, and the universal set (D) contains all possible elements under consideration.

mcqs.question: Two sets are said to be equal when:

options.A: They have at least one common element.
options.B: They contain exactly the same elements.
options.C: One is a subset of the other.
options.D: They have the same number of elements.

mcqs.answer: They contain exactly the same elements.
mcqs.explanation: Equality of sets requires that every element of one set appears in the other and vice‑versa, which is expressed in option B. Having a common element (A) or the same cardinality (D) does not guarantee equality, and being a subset (C) is a weaker condition.

mcqs.question: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {a, b, c}, which statement about A and B is true?

options.D: B is a subset of A.

mcqs.explanation: Sets A and B have the same number of elements (three each), so they are equivalent (same cardinality). They are not equal because their elements differ (A). They are not disjoint because disjointness concerns common elements, which is irrelevant here, and B is certainly not a subset of A.

mcqs.question: Which of the following notations correctly represents the empty set?
mcqs.explanation: The empty set is denoted by a pair of braces with nothing inside, i.e., {}. Option D shows the symbol ∅ inside braces, which is not standard notation. Options B and C contain an element, so they are not empty.

mcqs.question: A bag contains exactly five distinct balls. The collection of balls forms which type of set?
mcqs.explanation: Since the number of elements (five) can be counted and is limited, the set is finite. It is not infinite (A), not a singleton because it has more than one element (B), and not empty because it contains elements (D).

mcqs.question: Which statement about infinite sets is FALSE?

options.A: The set of natural numbers is infinite.
options.B: An infinite set can have a one-to-one correspondence with a proper subset of itself.
options.D: An infinite set does not have a last element.

mcqs.explanation: Statement C is false because some infinite sets, like the set of natural numbers, are countable. Statements A, B, and D are true properties of infinite sets.

mcqs.question: If a set S has exactly one element, which of the following must be true?

options.A: S is equal to the empty set.
options.B: S has exactly one subset besides itself.
options.C: The power set of S contains exactly two elements.

mcqs.answer: The power set of S contains exactly two elements.
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set S = {x} has two subsets: the empty set ∅ and S itself, so its power set has exactly two elements. Option A is wrong because S is not empty. Option B is incorrect because S actually has two subsets, not one. Option D is false unless the universal set is defined to contain all possible elements, which a singleton does not.
